_comment: Everything about YOUR channel lives here. Change values in this file rather than editing code - every script reads from it.

channel._handle_comment: Placeholder - set to the real handle once the channel exists.
channel.angle: I tell the true stories written into the planet - the eruptions, earthquakes, impacts, ice ages and slow collisions that built the world and will reshape it again - using the evidence scientists actually dug up: USGS, NASA and NOAA records, rock layers, ice cores and real footage.

video._comment: YouTube unlocks mid-roll ads at 8:00. 10-12 min is the sweet spot.
video._letterbox_comment: true adds 2.39:1 cinema bars over footage. Off by default: bars shrink the picture on phones, where most views happen.
video._outro_comment: Seconds of quiet, darkened hold on the last shot after the narration ends, for YouTube end screens (5s is the shortest end screen YouTube allows, 20s the longest). No text on it - the end-screen tiles and subscribe button sit over it.
video._intro_line_comment: Spoken before the script on every video (pipeline/narrate.py), so the word timings and storyboard include it. Empty string to drop it. The <break> tag is ElevenLabs syntax for a pause (a comma alone gave 0.03s).
video.intro_line: Hi, <break time="0.4s" /> welcome to another episode of the Earth Docs.

storyboard._comment: Shot planning, done after narration against the real word timings (pipeline/storyboard.py). All footage is planned as stock, cut where the narration changes subject; the stock stage fills a shot with as many short clips as it needs and only shots no library can show become AI. Cards are documentary question/fact cards and numbers are big key-figure shots - both capped, never captions.

charts3d._comment: GPT-6 Astra (OPENAI_API_KEY) writes a bespoke three.js/Remotion component for every chart shot, designed for that data and line of narration. Each must pass static rules, tsc, a full test render and a vision read-back of its numbers, or it falls back to the built-in chart (pipeline/charts3d.py). Big-number shots always use the built-in component. Prices per million tokens as of 14 Sep 2026; reasoning tokens bill as output.

visuals._comment: AI visuals via fal.ai (FAL_KEY) - the LAST resort on this channel, for scenes no camera recorded and shots no library could fill. Real footage from NASA, Wikimedia Commons, Pexels and Pixabay comes first (pipeline/stock.py). Every AI shot gets a keyframe; the highest-priority ones are animated until the estimate hits budget_usd, the rest get depth-parallax moves. Cached by content hash, so reruns cost nothing. PRICES CHECKED 20 Sep 2026 on fal.ai: minimax h3-max is $0.025/s at 480P, $0.04/s at 768P and $0.08/s at 1080P on a launch promotion that ends 30 Sep 2026, after which they become $0.05, $0.08 and $0.16 - double the usd_per_second below then, or the cap will under-count. Seedream lite is $0.035 an image at any size up to 3072x3072, so a sharper keyframe costs nothing extra. The video stays 1080p: the model cannot output 4K, and most real footage is 1080p, so a 4K render would upscale most of the screen for 4x the render time.

models._comment: Model IDs change. If a call 404s, check the provider's docs and update here - no code change needed.

writer._comment: Renamed Sept 2026: 'deepseek-v4-flash' became 'deepseek-flash' (V4.1 Flash) on 10 Sep. 'deepseek-v4-pro' reroutes to V4.1 Flash from 04:00 UTC on 14 Sep, so polish_model points there too until V4.1 Pro ships - then change polish_model back to it.

writer_fallback._comment: gemini-3.1-flash was retired; renamed to gemini-3.5-flash. Moved to gemini-3.8-flash on 15 Sep 2026: newer, and $0.75/$3.75 per 1M tokens vs 3.5 Flash's $1.50/$9.00 (introductory until 31 Dec 2026, then $1.50/$7.50).

vision._comment: Every picture the pipeline judges: stock contact sheets, AI keyframes, chart number read-backs and the thumbnail shrink test. Compared head to head on 7 real contact sheets from the Hunga Tonga build (19 Sep 2026): Gemini 3.8 Flash reads stand-in footage for things no camera can film (it passed satellite wave clouds 9/10 for a pressure pulse, and a sunset haze layer 7/10, where gpt-5.4-mini scored both below the 6/10 bar and sent the shots to AI). gpt-5.4-mini is stricter, 3s vs 7-14s per sheet and $0.0033 vs $0.007, and it is better on literal subjects (it found real underwater vent plumes Gemini missed) - but a rejected shot costs $0.04-$0.44 of AI generation, so the stricter model is the dearer one here. OpenAI is the automatic fallback when Gemini's prepaid balance runs out. Motion QA on AI clips is Gemini-only (OpenAI takes images only).

tts._comment: ElevenLabs eleven_multilingual_v2, one fixed voice and seed (Gemini TTS re-rolls the voice between calls). Voice is 'Liam' (TX3LPaxmHKxFdv7VOQHJ), chosen 19 Sep 2026 by the channel owner after listening to five-minute reads of the real script in six voices. It reads ~156 wpm at 125 Hz - the brightest and second fastest of the set, so a 13-minute script at 140 wpm lands nearer 11:45. Avoid voices with a custom-rate credit multiplier.
tts._style_comment: Prepended to every narration chunk as a spoken-style instruction (Gemini TTS follows it and does not read it aloud - verified 14 Sep 2026). Empty string for the voice's natural read (the default - a British RP style was tried 14 Sep 2026 and the natural read was preferred).

thumbnail._comment: Three concepts from the polish pass (or generated here for older runs) -> one image each with image_model -> Pillow draws the text and symbol -> a vision model runs the shrink test and ranks them. thumbnail.jpg is the winner; _b and _c are for YouTube Studio's Test & Compare.

safety._comment: review_only=true means the pipeline NEVER publishes. It builds the video and hands it to you. Flip to false only after your Phase 1 numbers say the format works.

targets._comment: From Phase 9.3 of the plan. Used by the topic engine as context.
